column1: # English translations of the one-sentence summary cell of each root README
# Consumed by translations/tools/build_root_readme.py. When upstream adds a new
# gallery row, add one line here; everything else in the row regenerates.
# An ellipsis at the end reproduces a summary that upstream itself truncates.

column2: Progressive dilatation and rupture risk driven by ECM degradation (MMP) in the aortic media together with chronic inflammation. Models beta-blockade, doxycycline, and anti-inflammatory targets.
A primary oesophageal motility disorder characterised by failure of the lower oesophageal sphincter (LES) to relax at the oesophagogastric junction plus absent peristalsis in the oesophageal body.

The commonest form of disproportionate short stature: an autosomal dominant disorder caused by a germline gain-of-function mutation in the transmembrane domain of FGFR3 (4p16.3) — G380R in about 97% of patients (roughly 80% de novo and associated with increased paternal age; homozygous ACH is lethal in the neonatal period).

A 55-ODE model that chains androgen-IGF-1/mTORC1 seborrhoea, the microcomedone reservoir created by infundibular hyperkeratinisation, C. acnes biofilm and antibiotic resistance, and NLRP3-IL-1beta inflammation into a lesion-transition sequence.
GH hypersecretion from a pituitary adenoma raising IGF-1. PK/PD of somatostatin analogues, pegvisomant, and dopamine agonists.

Writing the injury flux not as bacterial count but as the product of killing rate x bacterial count x inflammatory yield per organism shows by calculation that the product peaks immediately after the first antibiotic dose, and that the steroid which tightens the barrier also cuts vancomycin's CSF penetration along with it.

Loss of function of the HMBS (PBGD) gene leaves about 50% PBGD activity, so haem precursors (ALA, PBG) accumulate and drive neurotoxic acute attacks: ALA, a structural GABA analogue, competitively inhibits the GABA-A receptor while Fe2+-catalysed autoxidation generates ROS, causing mitochondrial failure, axonal degeneration, and autonomic, motor, and sensory neuropathy.

An integrated QSP model of the three subtypes — ischaemia-reperfusion (IRI), nephrotoxic (NTX), and sepsis-associated (SA-AKI). ATP depletion leads to mitochondrial failure, then apoptosis/necrosis/ferroptosis and loss of tubular cell viability (TCV), lowering GFR and raising NGAL/KIM-1.

Clonal leukaemic transformation of precursor B/T lymphocytes through multi-step genetic lesions (BCR-ABL1, ETV6-RUNX1, KMT2A rearrangement, hyperdiploidy, Ph-like, NOTCH1), characterised by bone-marrow-microenvironment-dependent chemoresistance (CXCL12/CXCR4, VCAM1/VLA-4) and resistance to glucocorticoid-receptor-mediated apoptosis.

FLT3/NPM1/IDH/DNMT3A mutations, the BCL-2 family, leukaemic stem cells, the marrow microenvironment, and epigenetic lesions. PK/PD of venetoclax (BCL-2), azacitidine, gilteritinib (FLT3), enasidenib (IDH2), and cytarabine.

After coronary occlusion the necrotic wavefront advances from endocardium to epicardium according to the difference between collateral flow and basal metabolic demand; reperfusion is both the treatment and a second injury; and infarct size is not an endpoint but the initial condition of a Laplace wall-stress remodelling bifurcation.
An acute inflammatory disease of the exocrine pancreas, diagnosed on two of three criteria (Atlanta 2012): serum lipase above 3x ULN, characteristic abdominal pain, and imaging findings.

Simultaneous collapse of the alveolar epithelial and endothelial barriers fills the lung with protein-rich oedema, reducing the ventilatable lung to a baby lung of 20-35%, on top of which the driving pressure, strain, and mechanical power applied by the ventilator feed back as VILI.
Autoimmune destruction of the adrenal cortex causing cortisol and aldosterone deficiency. Simulates the HPA axis and hydrocortisone/fludrocortisone replacement.

An oestrogen-dependent chronic disease in which endometrial glands and stroma invade the junctional zone (JZ) of the myometrium (20-35% of women of reproductive age, peaking peri-menopause): JZ hyperperistalsis (more than 4 waves/min perimenstrually, Kunz 1996) plus TIAR (Tissue Injury And Repair, Leyende…

Prefrontal cortex (PFC) dysfunction from reduced dopamine (DA) and noradrenaline (NE) neurotransmission. Risk genes (DAT1, DRD4, DRD5, SNAP25, COMT) reduce midbrain (VTA to PFC) DA synthesis and locus coeruleus (LC to PFC) NE tone, delaying cortical maturation of the PFC by about three years.
PKD1/2 mutation raises cAMP, driving cyst growth and loss of renal function. Effect of tolvaptan (V2 receptor antagonism) on TKV and eGFR.

Writing plasma mitotane not as a dose but as the overflow of a slowly filling fat reservoir shows by calculation that fat mass leaves the achieved concentration (Css) unchanged and alters only the time to reach it (tau), and that one and the same exposure is read simultaneously in three directions: efficacy, CYP3A4 induction, and neurotoxicity.
IL-1/IL-6/IL-18-mediated autoinflammation with fever, arthritis, and a steep rise in ferritin. Anakinra, canakinumab, and tocilizumab targets.

Ageing, genetics (CFH Y402H, ARMS2 A69S), and complement overactivation drive drusen formation and Bruch's membrane thickening, then RPE dysfunction and lipofuscin (A2E) accumulation, then MAC (C5b-9)-mediated RPE cell death, and finally geographic atrophy (GA, late dry AMD).

Plasma cell dyscrasia (MGUS to SMM to clonal plasma cells) with high CD38 expression hypersecretes monoclonal free light chains (FLC), which nucleate amyloid fibrils and amplify autocatalytically by elongation (beta-sheet polymer) and seeding, damaging the heart (LV thickening, diastolic dysfunction, raised NT-proBNP and hs-TnT), kidney (glomerular amyloid causing nephrotic syndrome, falling eGFR), liver (hepatomegaly, raised ALP), and autonomic…

A model that treats the ductal capacity ceiling created by bile duct paucity as an axis IBAT inhibitors cannot touch, showing that the ceiling on drug effect is set by the number of ducts rather than by bile acids.

A closed-loop structure in which drinking itself is an output of the model, separating the opioid-dopamine reinforcement arm from the GABA/glutamate allostatic negative-affect arm to reproduce why naltrexone and acamprosate move different clinical endpoints.

Ethanol to acetaldehyde (ADH/CYP2E1) with ROS generation depletes GSH and engages the Nrf2/KEAP1/ARE oxidative stress defence; gut dysbiosis raises intestinal permeability, letting LPS enter the portal circulation, and via TLR4/MD-2/CD14 activates NF-kB in Kupffer cells, then the NLRP3 inflammasome, then an IL-1beta/TNF-alpha/CXCL8 casca…

From the mass balance that inhibiting HPD with nitisinone does not reduce total flux through the tyrosine pathway but only changes its exit, the model derives the asymmetry that dose sets HGA while diet sets tyrosine, and the discrepancy between the fall in urinary and in serum HGA.

IgE- and Th2-mediated hypersensitivity to Aspergillus fumigatus colonising the airway forms high-attenuation mucus plugs whose interior becomes a sanctuary where antifungal concentrations fall tenfold, driving relapse and progression to central bronchiectasis.

An integrated QSP model of the IgE-mast cell axis (FceRI cross-linking to degranulation), the Th2 cytokine cascade (IL-4/5/13), and eosinophil kinetics. Includes the early response to histamine, PGD2, CysLTs (LTC4/D4/E4), and PAF, plus late eosinophil infiltration and the TSLP/IL-33 epithelial alarmin pathway.
Collapse of hair follicle immune privilege with IFN-gamma/IL-15 JAK-STAT signalling causing hair loss. Response to JAK inhibitors such as baricitinib.

SERPINA1 Glu342Lys (the Z allele) causes loop-sheet polymer accumulation of Z-AAT in the endoplasmic reticulum (gain-of-function hepatotoxicity) plus serum AAT insufficiency (below the 11 uM ELF threshold), leaving neutrophil elastase (NE) unrestrained and producing panlobular emphysema.

A hereditary kidney disease in which mutations in COL4A5 (X-linked, about 80%) or COL4A3/COL4A4 (autosomal), encoding the alpha3/alpha4/alpha5 chains of type IV collagen, prevent the mature alpha3-alpha4-alpha5(IV) network from forming in the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), leaving the mechanically fragile fetal alpha1-alpha2(IV) network in place.
Progressive cognitive decline from amyloid-beta deposition, tau neurofibrillary tangles, and neuroinflammation. Anti-amyloid antibodies (lecanemab, donanemab) and cholinesterase inhibitors.
Progressive degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons (SOD1, TDP-43, C9orf72). Riluzole, edaravone, and tofersen (SOD1).

Writing baldness as a problem of follicle size rather than follicle number, and allowing size to change only at the moment of exit from telogen, derives the 100 hairs shed per day, the flat finasteride dose-response, and the failure of late treatment all from the arithmetic of cycle time.

Renal fibrosis destroys the EPO-producing cells (REP) and blunts even the hypoxic stimulus, while inflammation and reduced renal hepcidin excretion create functional iron deficiency, producing ESA hyporesponsiveness.

Delayed cerebral ischaemia written as four consumers — large-vessel spasm, microvascular tone, microthrombosis, and loss of perfusion pressure — all eating into one arteriolar dilatory reserve, with oxyhaemoglobin released from subarachnoid blood as the driver.
Enthesitis and bone proliferation on the HLA-B27, IL-23/IL-17, and TNF axes. Effect of TNF and IL-17 inhibitors on BASDAI.

Cognitive restriction of intake creates a chronic negative energy balance with low leptin, free T3, and IGF-1 and raised cortisol; suppression of GnRH pulsatility produces hypothalamic amenorrhoea and reduced bone formation; and the model also simulates the refeeding syndrome risk created by the insulin surge during nutritional rehabilitation.

Separating the Top2b-DNA cleavage arm, which reads peak myocardial concentration, from the iron-ROS arm, which reads AUC, and modelling how compensatory hypertrophy masks reversible functional loss and irreversible myocyte loss, so that schedule, formulation, dexrazoxane, and concomitant trastuzumab can all be handled together.
Arterial and venous thrombosis and pregnancy complications caused by antiphospholipid antibodies. Anticoagulation (warfarin/heparin) and hydroxychloroquine.

Writing the quantity that tears the aorta not as pressure but as the product of false-lumen wall stress and dP/dt max derives arithmetically the conclusion that vasodilator monotherapy, which lowers pressure alone, can be worse than no treatment.

Valvular endothelial injury (shear stress, oxLDL, loss of NOTCH1) activates BMP-2/4 and TGF-beta1, driving osteoblastic transition of valvular interstitial cells (VIC; Runx2, Osterix, ALP up), raising the RANKL/OPG ratio, producing microcalcification (hydroxyapatite) then macrocalcification, reducing aortic valve area (AVA) and raising the transvalvular pressure gradient…

Activation of autoreactive CD8+ CTL (molecular mimicry, HLA-DR presentation) drives an IFN-gamma/TNF-alpha cytokine storm that kills HSC directly via FasL, perforin/granzyme B, and NF-kB/ROS/p53, depleting the haematopoietic stem cell pool and producing multilineage marrow failure (pancytopenia) with a hypocellular marrow (BM cellularity below 25%).

Treating a desmosomal mutation as lowering the load threshold at which the intercalated disc fails rather than as an amount of injury, the model writes myocyte loss as fatigue failure proportional to heart rate and to the fourth power of wall stress, and derives right-ventricular selectivity from the Laplace asymmetry.
Urate supersaturation without symptoms, and the risk of progression to gout and renal disease. Lifestyle measures and selective urate lowering (xanthine oxidase inhibition).
Skin barrier dysfunction with Th2 (IL-4/IL-13/IL-31) inflammation. Dupilumab, JAK inhibitors, and topical calcineurin inhibitors.
Atrial electrical and structural remodelling and re-entrant circuits. Rhythm/rate control and NOAC anticoagulation strategies.

Dysregulation of the complement alternative pathway (AP) — CFH/CFI/CD46 mutations, anti-CFH autoantibodies — leads to C3b accumulation and C5 convertase formation, then MAC (C5b-9) generation, then endothelial injury, and thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA): thrombocytopenia, MAHA, and acute kidney injury.
Encephalitis caused by antibodies against neuronal surface antigens such as the NMDAR. Immunotherapy with steroids, IVIG, plasma exchange, and rituximab.
Red cell destruction by warm IgG or cold IgM autoantibodies. Steroids, rituximab, and sutimlimab (anti-C1s).
T-cell-mediated hepatocyte injury with autoantibodies and hypergammaglobulinaemia. Steroid and azathioprine induction and maintenance.
IgG4-related lymphoplasmacytic infiltration and fibroinflammation. Steroid induction of remission and rituximab for relapse management.
AIRE mutation abolishes central tolerance, producing multi-organ endocrine autoimmunity. Models hormone replacement and immunomodulation.

Acid and bile reflux induce CDX2-mediated intestinal metaplasia and, through sequential CDKN2A and TP53 clonal evolution, progress to oesophageal adenocarcinoma; models acid-suppression and aspirin chemoprevention alongside radiofrequency ablation as eradication therapy.

A salt-losing tubulopathy model designed so that placing the same NaCl transport defect above the macula densa (TAL) gives Bartter and below it (DCT) gives Gitelman, with the rise in urinary PGE2 and the sign reversal of urinary calcium emerging as computed results.
Oral and genital ulcers and uveitis, with neutrophil- and IL-1-mediated variable-vessel inflammation. Colchicine, TNF inhibition, and apremilast.
DHT-mediated prostatic growth and smooth muscle tone causing lower urinary tract symptoms. Alpha-blockers and 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors.
Reduced beta-globin synthesis causing ineffective erythropoiesis, chronic haemolytic anaemia, and iron overload. Transfusion, iron chelation, and luspatercept (GDF11 inhibition).

Because the enterohepatic feedback sensor measures absorbed bile acid while the symptoms are made by the bile acid that overflows, freezing the feedback shows that malabsorption alone changes the colonic load by only 0.2% and produces no diarrhoea, and that SeHCAT and C4 read different lesions.

Alternating episodes of dopamine overactivity (mania) and serotonin/NE deficiency (depression). GSK-3beta overactivity lowers mTOR/BDNF and hippocampal neurogenesis; IL-6/TNF-alpha neuroinflammation; CLOCK/BMAL1 circadian disruption; and the CACNA1C (L-type Ca2+ channel) risk allele raising neuronal excitability.

FGFR3 mutation (about 60% of NMIBC) drives RAS/MAPK proliferation; TP53, RB1, and CDKN2A lesions mark high-grade MIBC; IFN-gamma-induced PD-L1 permits immune escape; and TGF-beta, Treg, and MDSC suppression.
Proliferative signalling by subtype (ER+, HER2+, TNBC). Endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitors, anti-HER2 agents, and immunotherapy.
Th2/eosinophilic airway inflammation and bronchial hyperresponsiveness. ICS, LABA, and anti-IL-5/IL-4Ralpha biologics.
The Cole vicious cycle of infection and inflammation, with neutrophil elastase destroying the airway. Airway clearance, antibiotics, and anti-inflammatory therapy.

A model formalising the disease as one in which the preterm infant alveolarisation programme is not destroyed by injury but arrested, permanently losing surface area within a closing developmental window. Caffeine, early hydrocortisone, vitamin A, and LISA are classified into exposure, delivery, and programme terms.
Subepidermal blister formation caused by anti-BP180/BP230 antibodies. Steroids, rituximab, and omalizumab.

A rare kidney disease in which genetic (CFH/CFI loss of function, CFB/C3 gain of function, CFHR5 duplication) or acquired dysregulation of the complement alternative pathway (a C3 nephritic factor autoantibody binds the C3 convertase C3bBb and blocks factor H-mediated decay) excessively stabilises the convertase, so that C3 breakdown products deposit predominantly in the glomerulus…

Cachexia is not starvation but a state in which three compensations have failed: the GDF-15/GFRAL arm that reduces intake and the STAT3/SMAD arm that switches on catabolism meet at muscle mass, while muscle quality fails separately, which is why lean mass and physical function dissociate.

Writing the two binding sites created by carbon monoxide with different time constants derives, from the asymmetry that measured carboxyhaemoglobin disappears quickly while cytochrome c oxidase binding releases far more slowly, both delayed neurological sequelae and the inconsistency of the hyperbaric oxygen trials.

A well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumour of ileal or jejunal origin (midgut NET, Ki-67 below 20%, WHO G1/G2) that, once it metastasises to the liver, releases 5-HT into the systemic circulation by portal bypass, producing the three cardinal features of carcinoid syndrome: (1) facial and cervical flushing (NK1, B2-bradykinin, H1 to eNOS-NO vasodilatation, with 5-HT2B contributing), (2) secretory…

A syndrome of tissue hypoperfusion caused by primary failure of the cardiac pump (SHOCK trial: 80% of AMI origin). Reduced LV contractility (EF below 30%, falling dP/dt), SV below 35 mL, and CI below 2.2 give MAP below 65, progressing through the five SCAI stages A to E.
Villous atrophy from the gluten-tTG immune response (HLA-DQ2/8). Gluten-free diet and glutenase drug candidates.

A disease in which release of the imprinted MKRN3 brake activates the KNDy pulse generator prematurely; because oestradiol raises growth velocity while simultaneously consuming growth plate reserve, the height gain from a GnRH agonist is determined by the bone age at which treatment starts.

The fourth commonest cancer in women worldwide (GLOBOCAN 2020: about 660,000 diagnoses and 350,000 deaths a year) and in practice universally attributable to persistent infection with high-risk HPV, especially HPV16/18: the viral oncoprotein E6 degrades p53 via the E6AP-mediated ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, abolishing the G1 checkpoint, while E7 binds pRb and releases E2F, so that the cell cycle…

Reading the point at which the botulinum toxin dose-response curve flattens not as pharmacological saturation but as a measurement of the fraction of muscle the injection actually reached, showing that the ceiling on sustained effect is set by geometry rather than by dose.

Recomposing the results of four randomised trials into three separated timescales — killing, the dormant reservoir, and myocardial remodelling — derives the paradox of the trypanocides from the fact that the axis blood qPCR measures is not the axis that produces cure.

A gene-dosage neuropathy in which a 1.4-Mb duplication at 17p11.2 gives three copies of PMP22; because the therapeutic target is restoration of the normal ratio rather than minimisation, it has an interior optimum with a wall on both the under- and the over-suppression side.

Writing the emesis endpoint not as a percentage but as the exponential of the integrated hazard of an additive drive derives, from the structure in which every antiemetic removes only one term from that sum, both the separation of the acute and delayed phases and the apparent synergy of the four-drug combination.

Cytotoxic chemotherapy kills proliferating marrow precursors rather than circulating neutrophils, and a fixed maturation delay line (MTT 89 hours) determines when that deficit becomes visible in blood, so the depth, timing, and duration of the nadir are governed by different parameters.

A peripheral neuropathy in which neurotoxic chemotherapy damages the DRG and distal axons and, through the SARM1 axon death programme, continues to worsen for weeks after the last dose; quantifies the therapeutic-index optimum of cumulative dose and the separation of Cmax from AUC.

Treating the delivered chemotherapy dose not as an input but as an output determined by bilirubin, neutrophil count, renal function, and performance status, a 54-ODE model describes how biliary drainage, which has no antitumour action of its own, changes survival.
Stone formation from biliary cholesterol supersaturation and gallbladder stasis. Dissolution therapy with ursodeoxycholic acid.
The H. pylori-Correa sequence (atrophy to intestinal metaplasia to dysplasia). Effect of eradication therapy and PPIs on mucosal recovery.

The disease is predicted by calibrating one thing only — NOX2 electron flux in the normal neutrophil phagosome — and the model shows that there is no threshold inside the phagosome, that the clinical correction threshold is created by organisms hiding inside phagocytes that were never killed, and that the mean DHR is not a sufficient statistic for infection risk.
HBV cccDNA persistence and immune-mediated liver injury. Viral suppression by nucleoside analogues and peg-IFN.

Perelson target-cell-limited viral dynamics (T/I/V ODEs) integrated with DAA PK/PD. Seven scenarios: SOF/LED, SOF/VEL, GLE/PIB, PEG-IFN/RBV. Models NS5B, NS5A, and NS3 inhibitor efficacy (epsilon_p/epsilon_i), CTL exhaustion, hepatic fibrosis (Metavir F-score), and HCC risk.

Treating HDV as an assembly line with two substrates — the genome the host makes and the HBsAg envelope HBV supplies — and classifying every drug by the flux it cuts: NTCP occupancy back-calculated from the fold rise in bile acids is only 0.71 at 2 mg, yet mitosis-mediated and cell-to-cell spread account for 40% of influx, which puts a ceiling on entry inhibition itself.

A model that writes serum potassium not as a reservoir but as the ratio of total body content to its intra/extracellular distribution: insulin and calcium remove not one mmol, only binders reduce the total, and an MRA does not raise potassium so much as pull the eGFR at which hyperkalaemia appears from 11 up to 21.
Reduced hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis output (TSH up, FT4 down). Dose-response of levothyroxine replacement.

A 63-ODE model that places 24-hour hyperarousal and the Spielman 3-P perpetuating loop on top of the two-process model and the VLPO-arousal flip-flop switch, reproducing the asymmetry that hypnotics target the switch while CBT-I targets the perpetuating loop.
Progressive loss of eGFR from glomerular hyperfiltration and fibrosis. Renoprotection with RAAS inhibition, SGLT2i, and finerenone.
Accumulation of CD19+CD5+CD23+ monoclonal B cells (the commonest adult leukaemia in the West).
Leukaemia driven by the BCR-ABL fusion tyrosine kinase. TKIs such as imatinib, T315I resistance, and treatment-free remission (TFR).

Writing chronic osteomyelitis not as a problem of antibiotic susceptibility but as two multiplicative penalties shows that diffusion loss into unperfused sequestrum compounds the collapse of growth-rate-dependent killing, and that surgery, rifampicin, and duration each act on a different object: the initial condition, the bactericidal ceiling, and the time to reach it.
Repeated injury activates pancreatic stellate cells, causing fibrosis and exocrine insufficiency. Enzyme replacement and pain management strategies.
Renal parenchymal scarring and loss of function from recurrent infection and reflux. Antibiotics and correction of reflux.

Injury to nasal and sinus epithelium releases the alarmins TSLP, IL-33, and IL-25, activating ILC2 and driving dendritic cell Th2 maturation, then an IL-4/IL-5/IL-13 cascade with IgE class switching, eosinophil recruitment, goblet cell hyperplasia, and mucus hypersecretion.

Writing haematoma volume not as a clot that failed to resorb but as a fixed point set by three terms of the neomembrane — exudation, rebleeding, and lymphatic absorption — derives from the asymmetry that surgery empties the stock while embolisation cuts the supply why the embolisation effect appears as an integral.

Incomplete fibrinolysis after pulmonary embolism leaves organised thrombus (mechanically fixed, raising PVR) plus secondary vascular remodelling (ET-1 up, NO down, PGI2 down, SMC proliferation), so total PVR rises, imposing RV pressure overload, hypertrophy, dilatation, and failure, with falling CO, SaO2, and 6MWD. Fibrinolysis is impaired by tPA deficiency, raised PAI-1, and abnormal fibrin cross-linking.

The IgE/FceRI-mast cell axis produces wheals, flare, and itch: autoantibodies (anti-FceRIalpha, anti-IgE) or autoantigen-IgE cross-link FceRI, mast cells degranulate (histamine, PGD2, LTC4), and an IL-31/IL-33/TSLP type-2 cytokine network sustains the urticaria.
Oedema and ulceration from valvular incompetence, raised venous pressure, and leucocyte trapping. Venoactive drugs (MPFF) and compression therapy.
Progressive or relapsing neuropathy from autoimmune destruction of myelin. IVIG, steroids, and plasma exchange.

Writing cochlear platinum as a reservoir rather than a concentration, and the route to it as a cascade from plasma to hair cell, derives the therapeutic window of thiosulfate given 6 hours later from a single time delay.

Falling GFR raises FGF23 steeply and lowers Klotho, inhibiting CYP27B1 and causing 1,25-(OH)2D3 deficiency; CaSR desensitisation then gives secondary hyperparathyroidism (raised iPTH) with hyperphosphataemia and hypocalcaemia, a disturbed RANKL/OPG balance and raised sclerostin producing osteodystrophy (osteitis fibrosa, adynamic bone, mixed), plus VSMC osteoblastic transition, MGP undercarboxylation, and fetuin-A…
Bile acid metabolism and nutrient niches wrecked by antibiotics permit spore germination and toxigenic colitis, and the microbial guilds that fail to recover after treatment ends drive recurrence.

Risk loci (HCRTR2, ADCYAP1, MTNR1A, CLOCK/BMAL1) plus a 5-18x family history and smoking activate the posterior hypothalamic grey matter, and an SCN/PVN/orexin circadian gate (peaking around 03:00) with the nocturnal trough in melatonin, testosterone, and cortisol activates the V1 trigeminal ganglion (trigeminovascular), dura, ICA, and pial vesse…

Reducing what an anti-CMV drug has to clear to a single threshold e* = 0.667 set only by doubling time and decay half-life, and placing beside it a second threshold the drug cannot move (E8* = 4.81/uL) together with the 57-fold clock created by the PCR sampling interval, so that prophylaxis, pre-emptive therapy, resistance, and dose reduction all become the same arithmetic.

A steroid-refractory disease in which monoclonal IgM cold agglutinin secreted by a clonal marrow B cell binds red cells at low temperature and activates the classical complement pathway, causing C3b-mediated extravascular haemolysis by hepatic Kupffer cells and C5b-9-mediated intravascular haemolysis. Rituximab, bendamustine, sutimlimab, and pegcetacoplan.

Integrates the APC/Wnt, KRAS/MAPK, and PI3K/TP53 pathways, the MSI-H and CMS subtypes, the tumour microenvironment (CD8, Treg, MDSC, TAM), and angiogenesis (VEGF/VEGFR). PK/PD of 5-FU, oxaliplatin, irinotecan (UGT1A1), bevacizumab (TMDD), cetuximab, and pembrolizumab (MSI-H).

Two diseases sharing one laboratory definition: the antibody-deficiency arm is quantitatively predicted by serum IgG concentration and solved by replacement therapy, whereas the immune-dysregulation arm (GLILD, autoimmune cytopenias, enteropathy) is unmoved by replacement and is what determines mortality.

Starting from the fact that beta-lactam killing is itself the release of cell wall and pneumolysin, a 38-ODE model treats fT above MIC and fAUC/MIC as integrated outcomes rather than parameters and describes how the sign of the net corticosteroid effect flips with bacterial susceptibility.

A chronic pain syndrome confined to one limb after fracture or surgery in which neurogenic inflammation, autoantibodies, sympathetic-afferent coupling, tissue hypoxia, spinal sensitisation, cortical reorganisation, and disuse bone loss overlap; separating the fast-decaying peripheral nodes from the slow behavioural-cortical loop and glial lock-in yields the therapeutic window (about 90 days) and the timing dependence of each drug.
21-hydroxylase deficiency causing cortisol deficiency and androgen excess. Glucocorticoid replacement and crinecerfont (CRF1 antagonism).

Writing the disease as a single number — residual beta-cell K_ATP conductance — and using the asymmetry that diazoxide multiplies that number while octreotide adds to the voltage divider, the diazoxide non-response of recessive K_ATP disease follows arithmetically.

Writing oocyte yield and OHSS in IVF stimulation as two readings of the same granulosa cell mass shows they cannot be separated by FSH dose, and that only the shape of the trigger separates them (maturation reads the leading edge of the signal, OHSS the area).
Airway and alveolar destruction from smoking-related oxidative stress and protease imbalance. Bronchodilation with LABA/LAMA and ICS.

Writing CFR not as a state variable but as the ratio of two flows derives the structure in which the same low CFR requires opposite drugs depending on whether it came from excessive resting flow (functional) or a limit on maximal hyperaemic flow (structural).
Transmural intestinal inflammation via Th1/Th17 and barrier permeability. Anti-TNF, anti-IL-12/23, and anti-integrin biologics.

Writing the disease with two different clocks — live yeast (days) and the capsular polysaccharide already dissolved in CSF (GXM, half-life about 13 days) — derives both the fact that every trial endpoint measures only the fast clock and the asymmetry that a single ergosterol node simultaneously produces the azole effect and the loss of the amphotericin target.
Chronic hypercortisolism from a pituitary ACTH adenoma (Cushing disease, 70%), ectopic ACTH (10%), or an adrenal adenoma (15%).

Placing one clone in three compartments — skin, blood, and lymph node — and separating mycosis fungoides from Sezary syndrome by tissue residency alone (CD69/CCR7), then deriving the gap in compartment-specific response rates and the separation of ORR from TTNT from the antibody skin partition coefficient and cutaneous NK density.
Raised mucus viscosity and chronic airway infection from CFTR mutation (dF508). CFTR modulators (elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor, Trikafta).

Massive activation of immune effector cells after CAR-T or bispecific antibody administration: a T-cell burst of IFN-gamma, IL-2, and GM-CSF drives M1 macrophage polarisation (JAK-STAT1) with a steep rise in IL-6 (the key driver), IL-1beta (NLRP3 inflammasome), and TNF-alpha — endothelial activation (iNOS to NO, vasodilatation, hypotension) and VEGF/ANG2-mediated vascular permeability causing hypoxia; and the blood-brain…

A model that derives, from one structure — presynaptic pathology is severe in all three ascending transmitter systems while the postsynaptic receptor landscape is remodelled in a different direction in each — the superiority of cholinesterase inhibitors, the poor levodopa response, neuroleptic sensitivity, and pimavanserin efficacy simultaneously, treating cognitive fluctuation as the variance of a bistable attentional state.

Reading a single rise in antibody through two pathways of opposite sign derives that defervescence and plasma leakage are two observations of the same event, and computes the structure in which the fluid dose-response is U-shaped because leakage stops only through shock.
Type I IFN- and complement-mediated microangiopathy of muscle and skin. Steroids, IVIG, and rituximab.
Covers AVP-D (central, AVP deficiency) and AVP-R (renal, AVP resistance) together, following the 2022 international working group renaming.

How a foot ulcer created by the overlap of neuropathy, ischaemia, and repeated pressure stalls in a protease-dominant, biofilm state; simulates offloading adherence, debridement, growth factors, antibiotics, revascularisation, and recurrence prevention together.

An acute metabolic crisis in which insulin deficiency creates two deficits with different numbers of exit routes: glucose has two (insulin-mediated disposal and renal excretion, whose conductance is extracellular fluid volume) while keto acids have only one, which saturates — so glucose normalises before ketones.

A diabetic microvascular complication progressing to CKD: hyperglycaemia (AGE, PKC, hexosamine, and polyol pathways) causes oxidative stress (Nox4, ROS) plus RAAS activation (AngII to intraglomerular hypertension), TGF-beta1 (Smad2/3, CTGF, ECM accumulation, glomerulosclerosis), and NF-kB inflammation (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, MCP-1, NLRP3), producing podocyte injury (nephrin, podocin, foot process…

Chronic hyperglycaemia accumulates in insulin-independent nerve, Schwann, and endothelial cells and converges on the four pathways of the Brownlee unifying hypothesis (polyol/AR, AGE/RAGE, PKC-beta, hexosamine) plus mitochondrial superoxide, PARP, and NAD+ depletion, causing vasa nervorum narrowing, basement membrane thickening, endoneurial hypoperfusion, and endoneurial hypoxia.

Hyperglycaemia acts through four biochemical pathways (polyol, hexosamine, PKC, AGE-RAGE) to produce oxidative stress, VEGF, and neuroinflammation, then structural retinal vascular lesions, then DME/PDR and visual loss: aldose reductase (AR) raises sorbitol and depletes NADPH; GFAT to O-GlcNAc raises TGF-beta and PAI-1; PKCbeta2 raises VEGF and NF-kB while lowering eNOS and raising ET-1; and me…
Ventricular dilatation, systolic dysfunction, and neurohormonal activation. Reverse remodelling with GDMT (ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i).
